page: Vultr vbm-32c-755gb-amd is a bare metal server configured with an AMD EPYC 9354P processor based on the x86_64 architecture. This dedicated hardware platform features 32 physical cores and 64 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 3.25 GHz. The system is equipped with 768.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, providing a resource density of 12.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is provided by a bundled 960 GB SSD, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present on this instance.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier performance in several key areas. The single-core CPU performance measured via stress-ng ranks in the top 10%, while multi-core performance is in the top 25%. Memory performance is highly competitive, with the Passmark memory score placing in the top 10% and uncached read-only memory bandwidth reaching 351.41 GB/sec. The system also demonstrates top-tier efficiency in LLM inference tasks, specifically achieving top 10% performance for prompt processing with a small 135M model and text generation with a medium 7B model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this bare metal server offers high resource density and dedicated hardware allocation, eliminating virtualization overhead. The combination of a high-capacity DDR5 memory array and 64 dedicated vCPUs makes it highly suitable for memory-intensive workloads. Recommended use cases include large-scale database operations, high-throughput web serving, software compilation, and memory-bound data processing tasks.
